test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.**

They said, "We shall visit the museum tomorrow."

options.text: They said they would visit the museum tomorrow.
They said that they will visit the museum the next day.
They said that they would visit the museum the next day.
They said they would be visiting the museum.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3) They said that they would visit the museum the next day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In indirect speech, when the reporting verb is in the past tense (“said”), the future tense **“shall/will”** usually changes to** “would.”**
 
• The word “tomorrow” also changes to **“the next day”** in reported speech.
 
• So, “We shall visit the museum tomorrow” becomes: ***They said that they would visit the museum the next day.***
 
• This option preserves both tense consistency and time expression change.

Therefore, the correct answer is– *They said that they would visit the museum the next day.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• They said they would visit the museum tomorrow. – Incorrect, because “tomorrow” should change to “the next day.”
 
• They said that they will visit the museum the next day. – Incorrect, because “will” should change to “would.”
 
• They said they would be visiting the museum. – Grammatically correct but incomplete; it omits the time reference, so it’s less accurate.
